artifacts.summary: Decides the typst-vs-lean4/formal/general boundary (typst owns presentation/quality of existing prose, not content origination), verifies via direct execution that the current keyword_overrides list cannot route chapter/manual tasks to typst and that adding 4 qualified phrases fixes it with no collisions; reproduces both chapter-quality-check.sh Rule 1.3 bugs (multi-file-manual root-doc bibliography, vendored .bib miscounting) live against Logos/Verification, recommends a nearest-ancestor-search + vendor-dir-exclusion fix, and audits the existing test suite (case-f valid unchanged, dirscan fixture unaffected under confirmed non-git mktemp fallback) plus a PASSED-banner WARN-tier qualifier for skipped BLOCKING rules.

memory_candidates.content: In this repo's task_type detection ladder (agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/lib/task-type-detect.sh), an extension's core weak-signal table (step 4) requires >=2 DISTINCT matched keywords per type to win. A type whose weak-signal entry has only one keyword (e.g. typst|typst) can NEVER resolve via step 4 alone, regardless of how many times that keyword appears in the description. The only fix point for such a type is its own manifest.json keyword_overrides (step 2), which is checked before and overrides step 4. Diagnose misrouting to a fallback type by checking whether the target type's weak-signal keyword count is >=2 before assuming keyword_overrides alone is the gap.

chapter-quality-check.sh's resolve_repo_root() falls back to the checked file's OWN directory (not any broader tree) when the file isn't inside a git worktree. mktemp -d workdirs (used by this repo's shell-script test fixtures) are confirmed NOT to sit inside any git repo in this environment (verified via git rev-parse --show-toplevel from a fresh mktemp -d). This means any fixture test relying on 'root' spanning multiple directories will silently collapse to a single-directory scope unless the test harness explicitly cds into or nests within a git-tracked path -- a subtlety worth checking before assuming a proposed ancestor-walk or root-relative fix will actually exercise multi-level resolution in the test suite.
